m1.typescript: m1 every tool call goes through the permission callback and the run is summarised

e1.typescript: e1 the options reach the cli as flags and the run starts in the project

e2.typescript: e2 file tools stay inside the project and away from secrets

e3.typescript: e3 bash is limited to a few commands and dangerous ones stop the run

e4.typescript: e4 a hook blocks a push before the permission callback is asked

e5.typescript: e5 the messages of a run fold into a summary

e6.typescript: e6 an error result still gives its summary and a crash is not hidden

e7.typescript: e7 denied calls are counted and the run still ends with a result

wrong-auto-approve.defect: lists the read tools in allowed_tools, so they run without the permission callback ever being asked

wrong-edit-in-readonly.defect: lets Write and Edit through in read-only mode

wrong-env-variants.defect: protects .env but not .env.local or other .env files

wrong-chaining-allowed.defect: allows a command that chains another with a semicolon or a pipe when it starts with a safe word

wrong-danger-no-interrupt.defect: denies sudo and rm -rf without interrupting the run

wrong-push-substring.defect: blocks any command that merely starts a word with git push, such as git pushd

wrong-no-turn-limit.defect: leaves max turns unset, so the run is not capped

wrong-raises-after-error-result.defect: lets the error that follows an error result escape, so a run that hit its limit has no summary

wrong-hides-crash.defect: swallows every error, so a process that died before any result looks like a run that ended

wrong-status-unmapped.defect: reports the raw result subtype instead of the course status for the turn limit

wrong-denied-capped.defect: counts at most one denied call however many the run had
